question: After entering the Flaming Mountains (火焰山), what is the first Spirit (精魄) absorbed?

rollouts.answer: The first spirit absorbed is 燧宝. First pickup explicitly labeled 精魄 at ~66990s ('燧宝 · 精魄').

db_evidence.notes: The only DB text anywhere containing the reference term '石父' is episodes:30sec:002156 (64680-64710s) and its parent episodes:3min:000359 (64620-64800s), both of which are unfiltered-range-queryable at the correct clue time. Confirmed via `memcli sql` that topic_facts and event_steps around 64650-64750 only record '虚空精 boss defeated ... loot orbs rise ... transitions to menu/inventory screen showing technique grid under 棍法 and 法术 tabs' — none of the structured tables (semantic_triples, topic_facts, event_steps, entities) ever use the literal word '精魄' or the name '石父' in connection with this event; entities table's only '精魄'-named row is an unrelated '石之精魄 (reward item)' first seen at 13020s. So the fact is present but only as raw caption flavor text describing a post-boss equipment-menu 'weapon card', never tagged/labeled as a spirit-absorption event anywhere in the DB, making it invisible to keyword search on '精魄' and requiring the agent to infer that a weapon-card name shown immediately after a boss kill represents the absorbed spirit.

root_causes: Literal-keyword SQL filters (LIKE '%精魄%'/'%吸收%'/'%拾取%'/'%灵魄%'/'%火焰山%') used by 3 of 5 rollouts systematically excluded the clue row, since its caption never uses those words -- it only says a 'weapon card showing 石父/石父之棍' appears in the skill menu after a boss kill.

In the 2 rollouts (2 and 4) that did run an unfiltered SQL query over the correct 64600-68200s window and thus had the 石父 row in their own context, the agent still failed to recognize it as the answer -- it read as ordinary equipment-menu flavor text rather than an explicit '精魄 absorbed' event, so it was skipped in favor of a later, more literally worded '(name)·(name) 精魄' item-pickup popup.

All 5 rollouts anchored their notion of 'entering the Flaming Mountains' to timestamps well after 64680s (66330s, 68100s+, 71600s+), so their clip_qa visual-verification calls never sampled frames near 64650-64750s and could not have visually confirmed 石父 even if they had suspected it.

Semantic_search queries phrased around 'spirit absorbed 精魄' consistently ranked later, explicitly-labeled pickup-popup segments (66990s, 68134s, 71824s) above the earlier weapon-card scene, since the embedding of a menu/equipment description is less semantically similar to 'absorbing a spirit' than an explicit on-screen '精魄' pickup notification.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly followed the skill-reading -> semantic_search -> run_sql -> clip_qa workflow and did visually verify their (wrong) candidate answers with clip_qa before submitting, so the failure is a retrieval/recognition problem, not an execution or tool-use failure.

Rollouts 2 and 4 did eventually run a correct, unfiltered time-windowed SQL query that returned the true clue row, showing the retrieval strategy of falling back to unfiltered scans of a narrow time window is capable of surfacing the evidence.
transferable_lessons: For 'first X after event Y' questions, always run at least one unfiltered SQL scan of the episodes table in a narrow window immediately following the anchor event, in addition to keyword-filtered scans -- literal-keyword LIKE filters can silently exclude the correct row if the caption phrases the fact differently than the question's terminology.

When a candidate row is retrieved but doesn't literally contain the question's key term (here '精魄'), don't discard it -- treat named items/cards shown in a post-boss-kill menu as a strong candidate for 'reward/absorbed' semantics and visually verify it with clip_qa before ruling it out in favor of a later, more literally-worded match.

Anchor 'entering X' events using multiple independent signals (fast-travel menu selection, map/loading transition, first combat encounter in the new area) rather than a single semantic_search hit, since all 5 rollouts converged on wrong entry timestamps that were 2000-7000s later than the true entry/first-event window.

Semantic search embeddings for 'spirit/item absorbed' can be biased toward explicit on-screen pickup-popup language and away from equipment-menu or weapon-card phrasing describing the same underlying event; cross-check top semantic hits against a plain unfiltered SQL scan of the same time range.
open_questions: Whether '石父' being shown as a 'weapon card' (石父之棍) rather than an explicit '精魄' pickup notification is itself an artifact of the captioning pipeline failing to recognize a spirit-absorption UI event, or whether that is genuinely how the game presents it (i.e. the reference answer requires outside knowledge of Black Myth: Wukong's 精魄 mechanic that isn't fully captured by the video captions).

Whether a differently-anchored search (e.g. explicitly searching entities/graph_edges for '石父' or running semantic_search directly on the string '石父') would have surfaced the row for the 3 rollouts that only used broader keyword filters; this was not tested.
